info.title: Strait API
info.description: Deep-linking + deferred-match API. Two keys, both in Dashboard → Get started: the **secret key** (`Authorization: Bearer st_live_…`, server-side only) for the link endpoints, and the **publishable key** (`publishableKey: "st_pub_live_…"` in the JSON body, safe in apps and websites) for /v1/match, /v1/referrer, /v1/resolve, /v1/open and /v1/event. Rotating the publishable key keeps the previous key working for 7 days; responses to the old key carry `Strait-Key-Deprecated: <ISO expiry>`, and after that it gets 401. Operations marked `x-internal: true` are used by the Strait dashboard or by Stripe and are not part of the public API. Errors are always JSON `{ "error": "…" }`: malformed JSON bodies get 400, unknown /v1 routes 404.

verified.description: true once Cloudflare reports the hostname and its certificate active and the ownership TXT record is in your DNS. Only then do links work on it.

status.description: live = serving your links. pending_dns = waiting for the CNAME and TXT records. issuing_certificate = DNS found, HTTPS certificate on its way. problem = needs attention (see message). not_created = saved while custom domains are read-only. unknown = the status could not be read right now.

message.description: Cloudflare's own words when something needs attention.

records.description: The DNS records to add at your DNS provider: one CNAME and the TXT records Cloudflare asks for.

slug.description: Unique among the workspace's active links (another workspace may use the same slug).

shortUrl.description: The link to share, on your workspace link domain: https://<handle>.strait.link/<slug>. Links live on their workspace's host; the bare root only answers a slug no other workspace uses.

tenantId.description: The workspace the link belongs to.

campaign.description: Analytics campaign; defaults to longUrl's utm_campaign.

passwordProtected.description: Present (true) when the link has a password.

blockedReason.description: Set when the link was disabled under the Acceptable Use Policy.

expiredAction.description: Where a tap goes once the link has expired. page = the "This link has expired" page (410). store = Google Play on Android / the App Store on iPhone (302, from your app configuration; the Play install referrer carries the tap); computers, and phones whose store is not configured, get the expired-link web page, else the expired page. url = 302 to expiredUrl. Absent/null = the workspace setting (Settings → When a link expires; default page).

expiredUrl.description: This link's expired-link web page (https); absent = the workspace's.

startsAt.description: epoch ms. Scheduled go-live: before it, taps get notLiveAction. Absent = live now.

notLiveAction.description: Where a tap goes BEFORE startsAt (the link is not live yet). page = a branded "Coming soon" page. store = Google Play on Android / the App Store on iPhone (302, from your app configuration); computers, and phones whose store is not configured, get notLiveUrl, else the page. url = 302 to notLiveUrl. Taps before go-live are not recorded and never billed; link-preview bots still get the preview card. Absent = page.

url.description: https; passes the same unsafe-destination check as longUrl

countryRules.description: Up to 5 rules, first match wins. When the tap's country (from Cloudflare, ISO 3166-1 alpha-2) is in a rule's countries, the rule's url replaces the web / fallback destination (iosFallbackUrl, androidFallbackUrl, desktopUrl, longUrl as a web page, the workspace fallback). Opening the app and the app-store hand-offs are unchanged. The country is used for this decision only and is never stored.

legacyHost.description: Imported from Firebase Dynamic Links: the old host (lower case, no https:// or path). Goes with legacyCode. When an app that keeps this host as an associated domain opens https://<legacyHost>/<legacyCode>, /v1/resolve finds this link by the old host + code before the slug, so the same code from two old hosts, or an old code and a newer slug, never clash. One active link per old host + code in a workspace (409 otherwise).

legacyCode.description: The old Firebase short code on legacyHost, exactly as it was (case-sensitive).

referralCode.description: Preview (referrals not switched on yet). Only in the POST /v1/links answer, and only when the code was saved. Not returned by the list, get or update endpoints yet.

longUrl.description: https only. The app receives its path + query as the in-app route.

iosFallbackUrl.description: iPhone without the app: this page instead of longUrl (https).

androidFallbackUrl.description: Android without the app (website mode): this page instead of longUrl (https).

desktopUrl.description: Desktop browsers go here instead of longUrl (https).

campaign.description: Campaign name for analytics. Defaults to longUrl's utm_campaign when omitted (and follows it when longUrl changes).

expiresAt.description: After this, the link stops opening its destination; expiredAction decides where taps go. Omit for never.

expiredAction.description: Where a tap goes once the link has expired. page = the "This link has expired" page (410). store = Google Play on Android / the App Store on iPhone (302, from your app configuration; the Play install referrer carries the tap); computers, and phones whose store is not configured, get the expired-link web page, else the expired page. url = 302 to expiredUrl. Omit to use the workspace setting (default page).

expiredUrl.description: https. Required with expiredAction url; with store it is where computers go. Passes the same unsafe-destination check as longUrl.

startsAt.description: Scheduled go-live. Before it, taps get notLiveAction; must be before expiresAt. Omit for live now.

notLiveAction.description: Where a tap goes BEFORE startsAt (the link is not live yet). page = a branded "Coming soon" page. store = Google Play on Android / the App Store on iPhone (302, from your app configuration); computers, and phones whose store is not configured, get notLiveUrl, else the page. url = 302 to notLiveUrl. Taps before go-live are not recorded and never billed; link-preview bots still get the preview card. Omit for page.

notLiveUrl.description: https. Required with notLiveAction url; with store it is where computers go. Passes the same unsafe-destination check as longUrl.

url.description: https; passes the same unsafe-destination check as longUrl

countryRules.description: Up to 5 rules, first match wins. When the tap's country (from Cloudflare, ISO 3166-1 alpha-2) is in a rule's countries, the rule's url replaces the web / fallback destination (iosFallbackUrl, androidFallbackUrl, desktopUrl, longUrl as a web page, the workspace fallback). Opening the app and the app-store hand-offs are unchanged. The country is used for this decision only and is never stored.

legacyHost.description: Imported from Firebase Dynamic Links: the old host (lower case, no https:// or path). Goes with legacyCode. When an app that keeps this host as an associated domain opens https://<legacyHost>/<legacyCode>, /v1/resolve finds this link by the old host + code before the slug, so the same code from two old hosts, or an old code and a newer slug, never clash. One active link per old host + code in a workspace (409 otherwise).

legacyCode.description: The old Firebase short code on legacyHost, exactly as it was (case-sensitive).

referralCode.description: Preview (referrals not switched on yet; until then the field is ignored). This link's referral code: 1 to 64 letters, digits, - or _. Every tap carries it unless the tap has its own ?strait_ref=; it comes back as `referralCode` in the deferred-match answer. Don't use an email address or phone number. Not accepted by the batch or update endpoints yet.

password.description: Optional: visitors must enter it before the link opens (link-preview bots still get the preview card). Stored hashed, never returned; the link shows passwordProtected: true.

taps.description: Taps on live links (not deferred-match entries, not taps on expired links).

billableTaps.description: Of those, the taps that count toward your plan (a repeat of the same tap within seconds is not billed).

appOpens.description: App opens reported by the SDKs that came from one of your links.

installs.description: Installs tied to one of your links (organic installs are not counted). The installs and first-open reports are merged: reports naming the same tap are one install, the same definition as the dashboard.

conversions.description: POST /v1/event events tied to one of your links (directly or through their tap).

revenue.description: Event values summed per currency code (upper case; '' when an event gave none). Currencies are never added together.

key.description: The group value: a UTC day (YYYY-MM-DD), a channel (whatsapp, instagram, direct…), a link id, or a platform (android, ios, desktop).

matchMethod.description: How it matched. 'clipboard' = a claimed paste-handoff token (POST /v1/handoff/claim). 'scored' is reserved for the scored iPhone matcher, which is not enabled yet.

confidence.description: Scored matches only (matchMethod 'scored'): 'high' or 'medium'. Null for every other answer of /v1/match.

clickId.description: When matched: the id of the tap this install came from. The SDKs remember it and send it with conversion events (/v1/event `clickId`).

referralCode.description: Preview (referrals not switched on yet). Present only when matched and the tap carried a referral code: the tap's ?strait_ref=, else its link's referralCode. Absent otherwise (never null). The SDKs pass it to your app as `referralCode` on the deferred link (contract B21).

deviceMatching.description: The workspace's Device matching switch (Dashboard Settings -> iPhone installs; opt-in, off by default).

pasteHandoff.description: The workspace's Paste handoff switch (opt-in, off by default). When true and this lookup found no match, the SDK checks the clipboard for the one-time handoff link and claims it (POST /v1/handoff/claim).

ios.description: /v1/match with platform 'ios' only: the workspace's current iPhone deferred-link choice (device matching and/or paste handoff, the customer's choice in the dashboard; opt-in, off by default), read live on every lookup so a change in the dashboard applies without an app release. The SDKs never store it (contract B19).

reasons.description: Why the matcher matched or refused, as short codes (never personal data). Exact matcher: exact_ext, exact_core, no_candidate, ambiguous (two identical-looking taps for different links: Strait refuses rather than guesses), race_lost (another lookup already took this tap), device_matching_off (the workspace turned iPhone install matching off). Paste handoff: clipboard, handoff_unknown, handoff_used, handoff_expired. Scored matches add signal codes (e.g. ipv6_64, ip_exact, asn, lang_full, dt_42s). New codes may be added; treat unknown codes as informational.

get.description: Without `limit`/`cursor`: every active link as a JSON array (unchanged). With either: one page `{ links, nextCursor }`, newest first; pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor` until it is null. `status=paused` lists paused links instead (turned off with DELETE, PATCH `isActive: false` or the dashboard; links disabled for abuse are not listed), always as pages.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size, 1–100 (larger values are capped at 100). Default 50 when paging.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque `nextCursor` from the previous page.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: `active` (default) or `paused`. Paused links come back as pages; turn one back on with PATCH `isActive: true`.

200.description: Links (array), or a page when limit/cursor is given

400.description: Invalid limit, cursor or status

post.summary: Create a link

201.description: Created: the link, with the shortUrl to share

400.description: Invalid field, or destination_blocked (a URL failed the unsafe-destination check)

402.description: Plan limit reached (this month's new links, or taps over twice the plan). Existing links keep working. Body: `{ error, reason: "links" | "clicks", upgradeUrl }` ("clicks" = the monthly tap limit).

409.description: An active link with this slug already exists in this workspace

429.description: New-account limit: a workspace younger than 24 hours can create 25 links. It lifts by itself; Retry-After says when. Body: `{ error: "new_account_limit", reason: "links", message, limit, resetsAt }`.

post.summary: Create up to 500 links in one call
post.description: For imports and migrations. Each item passes the same checks as POST /v1/links (slug rules, https destinations, the unsafe-destination check, plan limits) and gets its own result; a bad item never fails the batch. A slug already used in the workspace (or earlier in the same batch) is a per-item 409, so re-running an import is safe. The response is 200 whenever the request itself is valid: read `results[i].ok`. Items past a plan limit get 402.

200.description: One result per item, in order, plus totals

status.description: What POST /v1/links would have answered: 201, 400, 402 or 409.

results.error: slug already exists in this workspace

400.description: `links` is missing, empty, or has more than 500 items

parameters.name: slug
parameters.description: The link's slug: the part after your link domain, e.g. `summer`

200.description: The link (with shortUrl)

404.description: No active link with this slug in the key's workspace

patch.description: Send only the fields to change. null clears expiresAt (never expires), expiredAction (back to the workspace setting), expiredUrl, startsAt (live now), notLiveAction (the coming-soon page), notLiveUrl and countryRules (null or [] = none; a list replaces all rules). `isActive` is sent on its own: `false` pauses the link (same as DELETE). `true` answers the active link with this slug if there is one (safe to retry; check its longUrl), else turns the most recently paused one back on (taps follow within 30 seconds, like any edit). A link disabled for abuse cannot be turned back on (409 link_blocked).

parameters.name: slug
parameters.description: The link's slug: the part after your link domain, e.g. `summer`

expiredAction.description: Where taps go once the link has expired (see NewLink); null = the workspace setting.

expiredUrl.description: https; required when expiredAction is url.

startsAt.description: Scheduled go-live (see NewLink); null = live now.

notLiveAction.description: Where taps go before startsAt (see NewLink); null = the coming-soon page.

notLiveUrl.description: https; required when notLiveAction is url.

isActive.description: Send alone. false = pause, true = turn the paused link back on.

url.description: https; passes the same unsafe-destination check as longUrl

countryRules.description: Replaces all country rules (see NewLink); null or [] removes them.

200.description: Updated

400.description: Invalid field, isActive sent with other fields, or destination_blocked (a URL failed the unsafe-destination check; with isActive: true the link stays paused)

404.description: Not found (with isActive: true: no paused or active link with this slug)

409.description: isActive: true refused: link_blocked (disabled for abuse) or slug_in_use (the database refused: a link created at the same moment, or the same Firebase link is on)

parameters.name: slug
parameters.description: The link's slug: the part after your link domain, e.g. `summer`

404.description: No active link with this slug in the key's workspace

get.summary: Get a branded QR code for a link
get.description: A print-ready QR code (PNG or SVG) that opens the link's short URL. It uses the workspace's QR style (Dashboard → Settings → QR codes: colour, background, app icon in the middle); query parameters override it for this one code. By default the code adds `utm_source=qr`, so scans show as the **qr** channel in analytics (an existing utm_source on the link is kept). The code must be darker than its background with a contrast of at least 3:1, or the request is refused with 400. With a logo the code uses error correction H. The logo is the app icon from Settings: PNG, JPEG or WebP in SVG codes, PNG only in PNG codes; X-Strait-Qr-Logo says whether it was embedded. Rate limit: 60 codes a minute per workspace; PNG renders also share a server-wide budget (large PNGs may get 429, retry or use SVG).

parameters.name: slug
parameters.description: The link's slug: the part after your link domain, e.g. `summer`

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Image format

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: Width and height in pixels

parameters.name: margin
parameters.description: Quiet zone around the code, in modules

parameters.name: color
parameters.description: Code colour as hex (`1f2937`, or `%231f2937`). Default: the workspace's QR colour, else black.

parameters.name: background
parameters.description: Background colour as hex. Default: the workspace's QR background, else white.

parameters.name: logo
parameters.description: Put the app icon in the middle. Default: the workspace's QR setting.

parameters.name: track
parameters.description: Add utm_source=qr so scans count as the qr channel

parameters.name: download
parameters.description: true: Content-Disposition attachment (a browser saves the file)

parameters.name: tenantId
parameters.description: Dashboard sessions only: the workspace id (a secret key already names its workspace)

200.description: The QR code

X-Strait-Qr-Url.description: The exact URL encoded in the code

X-Strait-Qr-Logo.description: embedded · off · no_icon (no app icon in Settings) · unavailable (icon unreachable or not PNG/JPEG/WebP ≤ 512 KB) · png_needs_png_icon (use format=svg, or a PNG icon)

image/svg+xml.example: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="1024" height="1024" viewBox="0 0 37 37" shape-rendering="crispEdges"><rect width="37" height="37" fill="#ffffff"/><path fill="#1f2937" d="M2 2h7v1h-7z…"/></svg>

400.description: Invalid parameter, or colours that would not scan (code lighter than the background, or contrast under 3:1)

401.description: Missing or invalid secret key / session

404.description: No active link with this slug in the workspace

429.description: More than 60 codes a minute for this workspace (Retry-After: 1), or PNG rendering is busy server-wide (Retry-After: 2; SVG is not limited by it)

get.description: Taps, app opens, installs, conversions and revenue for your workspace in [from, to), for every link or one, optionally grouped by day, channel, link or platform. The numbers use the same definitions as the dashboard. Each item counts at its own time (a tap at its tap time, an install at its install time); days are UTC. Secret key only (a publishable key gets 401). At most 92 days per call and 30 calls a minute per workspace (429 with Retry-After).

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Inclusive start: ISO date (2026-10-01, UTC), ISO date-time or epoch ms. Default: 30 days before `to`.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Exclusive end, same formats. Default: now.

parameters.name: link
parameters.description: Only this link: an active link's slug, e.g. `summer`.

parameters.name: group
parameters.description: Split the numbers into rows. Default none (totals only).

200.description: Totals, plus one row per group value (biggest first; by date for group=day). `rows` is empty for group=none.

link.description: The slug asked for, or null for every link.

400.description: Bad from / to (or a range over 92 days), unknown group, malformed link

401.description: Missing or invalid secret key, or a publishable key

404.description: No active link with this slug in the key's workspace

429.description: Over 30 calls a minute for this workspace

get.description: Where your workspace stands against its plan this calendar month (UTC): billed taps and new links, and what the plan includes (null = no limit). `level` is ok, warn from 80 % of the included taps, over from 100 %. Over your plan, links and deferred matching keep working: nothing here ever stops a redirect. `new_links_paused` is true at twice the included taps or at the plan's new-link limit; creating a link then answers 402 until you upgrade or the month ends. Secret key only (a publishable key gets 401); 30 calls a minute per workspace (429 with Retry-After).

200.description: This month's usage, the plan and the over-limit flags.

plan.description: The plan in effect (a canceled plan, or one past due for over 7 days, is free).

401.description: Missing or invalid secret key, or a publishable key

429.description: Over 30 calls a minute for this workspace

get.description: Preview, not switched on yet: until referrals are switched on for the API, this answers 404 like any unknown /v1 route, and the fields may change before then. For each referral code in [from, to): the taps that carried it and the referred installs (an install that opened and matched a tap with that code, at most one per tap). A tap counts at its tap time, a referred install at its first open; days are UTC. Most conversions first. Secret key only (a publishable key gets 401). At most 92 days per call and 30 calls a minute per workspace (429 with Retry-After). Each new referred install also fires the `referral.converted` webhook.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Inclusive start: ISO date (2026-10-01, UTC), ISO date-time or epoch ms. Default: 30 days before `to`.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Exclusive end, same formats. Default: now.

200.description: Totals plus one row per referral code

preview.description: Always true while referrals are a preview.

codes.description: Codes with at least one tap or referred install in the range.

400.description: Bad from / to (or a range over 92 days)

401.description: Missing or invalid secret key, or a publishable key

429.description: Over 30 calls a minute for this workspace

post.summary: Deferred-match lookup (first app open after an install)
post.description: Called once by the SDKs on the first launch after an install, to find the tap that led to it. On iPhone it compares coarse device signals (screen, language, time zone, network) with recent taps of this workspace and answers only when exactly one tap fits; ambiguous cases are refused, never guessed. Android uses POST /v1/referrer (Play Install Referrer) instead. Rate limited per IP.

record.description: false = a read only (SDK checkDeferred): answer the match, record no install, open or webhook. Omit for the real first-launch check.

200.description: Match result

400.description: platform and the device fields are required

post.summary: iPhone paste handoff (opt-in): claim a one-time handoff token (exact, single use)
post.description: Only when the workspace turned on Paste handoff (Dashboard Settings -> iPhone installs; opt-in, off by default); the SDK reads it live from the ios.pasteHandoff field of POST /v1/match and checks the clipboard only then. The token comes from the handoff link https://<link host>/h/<token> that the tap page copied; it belongs to one tap of this workspace, works once and expires after 24 hours. When it does not match, nothing is recorded and the SDK falls back to POST /v1/match with the same openId. Rate limited per IP.

openId.description: The open id of this first app open: the claim also reports the open.

200.description: Claim result: matchMethod clipboard with clickId, or matched:false with reason handoff_unknown, handoff_used, handoff_expired or not_found

400.description: token is not a handoff token

post.summary: Record an in-app store sheet tap and get what keeps the deep link (new)
post.description: New. Called by the SDKs (Strait.openStoreSheet) just before an app shows the app store inside itself: Google Play inline install on Android, SKOverlay / SKStoreProductViewController on iPhone. Records a tap with sent_to 'store_sheet' (not billed while the store sheet is new). Android gets the Play Install Referrer string (strait_link + strait_click, matched exactly by /v1/referrer); iPhone gets the App Store id, the link's campaign as the ct token and, with Paste handoff on, a one-time handoff link. This works inside your own app only; a link tapped inside another company's app cannot open a store sheet there.

url.description: A short link of the key's workspace

deviceClass.description: What the app runs on (iPad = tablet); phone when not sent

200.description: ok:true with the store details, or ok:false with reason (not_found, disabled, expired, not_live, password_protected)

400.description: Bad url or platform

post.summary: Deferred-match resolution from Android Play Install Referrer (deterministic)

record.description: false = a read only (SDK checkDeferred): answer the match, record no install, open or webhook. Omit for the real first-launch check.

200.description: Match result

post.summary: Turn a short link that opened your app into its destination
post.description: Called by the SDKs when a verified short link (App Link / Universal Link) opens the app directly. With `openId` the lookup also records the app open and the tap (once per openId); `recorded:false` means retry the report via /v1/open. Old Firebase links (contract B22): on a host that is not Strait's (e.g. acme.page.link), a link imported with that legacyHost + legacyCode is matched first; a long link (`https://<x>.page.link/?link=…`) answers `reason: long_link` (current SDKs read its link= on the device instead).

deviceClass.description: What the app runs on (iPad = tablet), stored on the tap this open records. iPadOS Safari sends a Mac user agent, so browser taps from an iPad count as desktop.

200.description: { matched, longUrl?, linkId?, slug?, clickId?, reason?, recorded? } — reason: not_found | expired | not_live (scheduled, before go-live) | password_protected | long_link (an old page.link long link: read its link= in the app). clickId (when matched) is the id of the tap this open recorded; send it with conversion events (/v1/event `clickId`).

recorded.description: With openId: whether the open was recorded (false = retry via /v1/open).

400.description: url is not a short link

post.summary: Report that a link opened the app
post.description: Sent by the Strait SDKs for every link open they cannot report through /v1/resolve, /v1/referrer or /v1/match (browser hand-offs, your own https links), and to retry any open report that failed to send. De-duplicated by `openId`.

url.description: The opened URL (only host + path are stored)

deviceClass.description: What the app runs on (iPad = tablet), stored on the tap this open records. iPadOS Safari sends a Mac user agent, so browser taps from an iPad count as desktop.

202.description: Recorded (`duplicate: true` when this openId was already recorded)

400.description: Invalid fields

429.description: Rate limited: per IP (60 burst, 1 a second) or per workspace (600 burst, 10 a second; Retry-After). The SDKs keep the report and retry it, de-duplicated by openId

post.summary: Read old page.link codes while Google still answers (dashboard)
post.description: Called by the dashboard importer with the signed-in user's session token (owner, admin or member; never a secret key). For each old https://<x>.page.link/<code>, reads Google's Firebase Dynamic Links debug page (?d=1), an UNDOCUMENTED format that works only while Google still answers, and returns the old long link and its parameters (link, afl/ifl/ofl, st/sd/si, utm_*). Before any code is read, the host's apple-app-site-association or assetlinks.json must name the workspace's own iOS app id (Team ID + bundle ID) or Android package. About 1 Google request per second and 500 a day per workspace; answers cached for an hour.

urls.description: https://<x>.page.link/<code> links, or bare codes with host

200.description: `{ results: [{ input, host, code, status: found | not_found | unreadable | not_your_app | invalid | error | limited, longLink?, fields?, message }], ownership: [{ host, ok, via?, message }], note }`

400.description: Bad urls/host, or no_app_config (add your iOS or Android app ids first)

403.description: A viewer, or a secret key

429.description: A rescue is already running for this workspace

post.summary: Start the one-step Firebase migration (dashboard)
post.description: Called by the dashboard with the signed-in user's session token (owner, admin or member; never a secret key). Give the old domain (`host`, e.g. acme.page.link), and/or `text`: a pasted list of old short links or codes, a CSV (short_link + destination and FDL parameter columns), or a JSON export (FDL REST `dynamicLinkInfo` objects or `{ shortLink, longLink }`). With a host, the engine also looks the host up in the Internet Archive's public index. Every old link becomes one item per (workspace, host, code); the engine rebuilds them in the background: from the destination given, else (page.link only, and only when the host names the workspace's own app) from Google's undocumented debug page. A second call while a migration is open adds to it; re-runs never make a second link.

text.description: List, CSV or JSON export as text (up to 20,000 links)

discover.description: Search the Internet Archive for the host (default true when host is given)

200.description: Added to the open migration: `{ migration, added, requeued, format, skipped, skippedCount }`

201.description: Started: `{ migration, added, requeued, format, skipped, skippedCount }`

400.description: Nothing to migrate, bad host, or too many links

403.description: A viewer, or a secret key

post.summary: Record a conversion / revenue event
post.description: From an app or website send `publishableKey`; from a server you may instead authenticate with the secret key as a Bearer token. `clickId` names the tap the conversion came from: every tap gets a unique id (a UUID, sent with the tap's redirect and passed to your app with the open), which the mobile SDKs remember from the attributed app open and attach for 7 days. It is kept only when it is a tap of this workspace; otherwise it is ignored and the event is still recorded. Each new event (not an eventId retry) is sent to your webhooks subscribed to `app.event`, with `data` and `sentWith` (publishable_key or secret_key: trust revenue sent from your server). Webhook sends for events sent with the publishable key are capped per workspace (600 burst, then 10 a second): past that, they are still recorded but not sent. Events sent with the secret key are not capped.

linkId.description: Optional: with a known clickId it is filled in from that tap

clickId.description: The id of the tap this conversion came from (the mobile SDKs fill it in)

eventId.description: Optional idempotency id, e.g. your order id: a retry with the same eventId is accepted but stored once

data.description: Optional custom key-values (at most 20, 2 KB as JSON) passed to the app.event webhook. Not stored with the event; kept 30 days with the webhook delivery. Do not send personal data your receiver does not need.

202.description: Accepted. `clickId` echoes the tap id that was stored, or null when none was given or it was not a tap of this workspace.

linkId.description: The linkId kept for this event: yours if it is one of your links, else the clickId tap's link; null when neither (unknown ids are dropped, the event is still recorded)

post.summary: Send a test event to a webhook
post.description: Delivers a `ping` event to the webhook right now (even if paused) and returns the receiver's HTTP status and the time it took (never its response body). Not stored or retried. Every delivery is signed: `X-Strait-Signature: t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<t>.<raw body>" with the webhook secret>` — recompute it and refuse timestamps more than 5 minutes old. It is the only signature header. Other headers: X-Strait-Event, X-Strait-Delivery (stable across retries — de-duplicate on it), X-Strait-Attempt. Events: link.clicked, app.opened, install.matched, referral.converted and app.event (POST /v1/event). Webhook URLs must be public https endpoints: private, loopback, link-local and CGNAT addresses are refused when saved and again at every delivery, when the connection is made (after DNS resolution).

post.description: Re-queues one delivery (typically `failed`, after all retries) and sends it right away to the webhook's current URL, with the same X-Strait-Delivery id. Its attempt count starts over, so it gets the full retry schedule again. Refused (409) when it was already delivered, or while it is being sent (younger than 2 minutes, or claimed by a worker right now).
